answer.query: Does PEP 484 require Python to enforce type hints at runtime?
answer.text: No. PEP 484 explicitly states that Python will remain a dynamically typed language, and the authors have no desire to ever make type hints mandatory, even by convention. No type checking happens at runtime under this proposal; instead it assumes a separate off-line type checker that users can run voluntarily, acting like a powerful linter.

answer.query: Why does PEP 526 favor annotation syntax over type comments for parsing?
answer.text: Because type comments aren't actually part of the language, so a tool wanting to parse them needs a custom parser instead of simply being able to use Python's built-in `ast` module, as would be possible with dedicated annotation syntax.
